children: Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRNA) raised $2.6B via 2032 zero‑coupon convertibles and a hedge overlay to limit dilution as it funds oncology programs including intismeran — a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine — while FDA cleared updated Spikevax/mNEXSPIKE for JN.1 XFG and shares jumped after an upgrade.
: Moderna (MRNA) issued $2.6B convertible notes due 2032, 0% coupon, convertible ~ $210.58/share (~47.5% premium). Proceeds for capped calls, general corporate uses, oncology and debt paydown.
: FDA approved Moderna’s 2026–27 Spikevax and mNEXSPIKE updated for JN.1-lineage XFG. Age and risk-based authorizations apply; Moderna says doses available in coming days.
: Moderna (MRNA) surged after Wolfe Research upgraded the stock, with intraday gains near 11–14%, pushing price toward $154–$159; Wolfe offered no price target.
Moderna Hedge Overlay To Offset Dilution
: Moderna (MRNA) disclosed a hedge overlay buy to offset dilution; the hedge's initial cap was set at a 175% premium to the stock price at pricing.
: Moderna (MRNA) says intismeran is a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine targeting up to 34 neoantigens per patient, with about a six-week manufacturing window from tumor sample to delivery.

title: Weekly Recap: Convertible notes and FDA approval of Spikevax and mNEXSPIKE
